LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon GuardDuty vs. Amazon Inspector vs. Amazon Macie?
column2:
GuardDuty: Intelligent threat detection (CloudTrail, DNS, VPC Flow Logs).
Inspector: Automated vulnerability scanning (CVEs/network exposure on EC2, ECR, Lambda).
Macie: ML discovery of sensitive data / PII inside Amazon S3.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon CloudWatch vs. AWS CloudTrail vs. AWS Config?
column2:
CloudWatch: Performance metrics, logs & alarms (CPU, latency).
CloudTrail: API audit log (who called which API, when, from where).
Config: Resource configuration history & compliance rules over time.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS Security Hub vs. Amazon Detective?
column2:
Security Hub: Central dashboard that aggregates & prioritizes security findings across accounts/services + compliance checks.
Detective: Visual graph tool to investigate and find the root cause of a security incident.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS Shield vs. AWS WAF vs. AWS Firewall Manager?
column2:
Shield: Managed DDoS protection (L3/L4; Advanced adds SRT + cost protection).
WAF: Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS filtering (SQLi, XSS, geo/IP rules).
Firewall Manager: Centrally enforces WAF/Shield/SG rules across AWS Organizations.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS KMS vs. AWS CloudHSM vs. AWS Secrets Manager vs. ACM?
column2:
KMS: Multi-tenant managed encryption keys.
CloudHSM: Dedicated single-tenant FIPS hardware key appliance.
Secrets Manager: Stores & auto-rotates DB passwords/API keys.
ACM: Provisions & auto-renews SSL/TLS HTTPS certificates.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS IAM Identity Center vs. Amazon Cognito?
column2:
IAM Identity Center: Internal workforce SSO (employees accessing multiple AWS accounts & business apps).
Cognito: External customer/app user sign-up/sign-in (mobile/web, Google/Apple/Facebook).

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Security Group vs. Network ACL (NACL)?
column2:
Security Group: Instance level · Stateful · Allow rules ONLY.
NACL: Subnet level · Stateless · Allow AND Deny rules (can block a specific bad IP address).

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon CloudFront vs. AWS Global Accelerator?
column2:
CloudFront: Caches HTTP/HTTPS content (video, images, web assets) at Edge Locations.
Global Accelerator: Accelerates non-HTTP / TCP & UDP apps via 2 static Anycast IPs over AWS backbone (no caching).

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS Site-to-Site VPN vs. AWS Direct Connect?
column2:
Site-to-Site VPN: Encrypted over public internet, quick setup, lower cost, variable bandwidth.
Direct Connect: Dedicated private physical fiber, consistent high bandwidth & low latency, weeks to provision, not encrypted by default.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: VPC Peering vs. AWS Transit Gateway?
column2:
VPC Peering: Direct 1-to-1 private link between two VPCs (non-transitive; gets messy at scale).
Transit Gateway: Central hub-and-spoke router connecting dozens/hundreds of VPCs and on-premises networks cleanly.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon S3 vs. Amazon EBS vs. Instance Store vs. Amazon EFS vs. Amazon FSx?
column2:
S3: Regional object storage.
EBS: Persistent single-AZ block volume for 1 EC2.
Instance Store: Ephemeral local NVMe (lost on stop).
EFS: Multi-AZ serverless Linux NFS file system.
FSx: Managed Windows SMB / Lustre / ONTAP / OpenZFS file systems.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon RDS vs. Amazon Aurora vs. DynamoDB vs. Redshift vs. Athena?
column2:
RDS: Managed SQL (OLTP).
Aurora: Cloud-native high-speed MySQL/Postgres (6 copies / 3 AZs).
DynamoDB: Serverless NoSQL (ms latency).
Redshift: Petabyte SQL Data Warehouse (OLAP).
Athena: Serverless SQL queries directly on S3.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS Lambda vs. AWS Fargate vs. AWS Elastic Beanstalk vs. Amazon Lightsail?
column2:
Lambda: Event-driven serverless functions.
Fargate: Serverless compute for containers (ECS/EKS).
Elastic Beanstalk: Managed PaaS for deploying web app code.
Lightsail: Simple fixed-monthly-price VPS for small websites/blogs.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon SQS vs. Amazon SNS vs. Amazon EventBridge vs. AWS Step Functions?
column2:
SQS: Decoupling message queue (pull).
SNS: Pub/sub push fan-out alerts.
EventBridge: Serverless event bus connecting AWS & SaaS apps.
Step Functions: Visual multi-step workflow orchestration.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: AWS Pricing Calculator vs. Cost Explorer vs. AWS Budgets vs. CUR?
column2:
Pricing Calculator: Estimate cost before launch.
Cost Explorer: Visualize historical spend + 12-mo forecast.
Budgets: Custom threshold alerts (actual or forecasted).
CUR: Most detailed raw line-item billing files to S3.

column1: LOOK-ALIKE: Amazon WorkSpaces vs. Amazon AppStream 2.0 vs. Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser?
column2:
WorkSpaces: Full persistent cloud virtual desktop (VDI).
AppStream 2.0: Stream specific desktop apps to a browser.
WorkSpaces Secure Browser (formerly WorkSpaces Web): Managed secure browser for internal web apps.

column1: 2026 ERRATA TRAP: Name 3 outdated myths still found in free GitHub/old practice exams that are FALSE on the real 2026 exam.
column2:
1. Pen-testing requires prior AWS approval: FALSE — permitted services (EC2, RDS, S3/CloudFront, Lambda, etc.) do NOT require prior approval.
2. Bid on EC2 Spot Instances: FALSE — no bidding since 2017; supply/demand pricing + 2-min warning.
3. Simple Monthly Calculator / TCO Calculator: RETIRED — use AWS Pricing Calculator (and Migration Evaluator).

column1: EXAM RULE: What answer pattern does the CLF-C02 phrase least operational overhead or minimal management almost always signal?
column2: Choose the most managed or serverless AWS service (e.g., Lambda over EC2, Fargate over self-managed EKS nodes, DynamoDB / RDS / Aurora over DB-on-EC2, Athena over self-managed Hadoop, S3 over EBS file servers).
